body.statement: For fixed \(\mathcal A\), when \(L=0\) the feasible refinement is the translation closure of one finite static ADMG on \(V\), and \(\gamma=0\).  The certified partial \(\operatorname{TID\text{-}SCG}(H,0,\mathcal A,X,Y,0,x,y)\) makes one ordinary ID call on the relevant ancestral subgraph.  If ID succeeds, it returns \(\operatorname{SUCCESS}(F)\), where \(F\) is the ordinary ID functional on the common product alphabet; if ID fails, it returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\).  No fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is claimed on the failure branch.
body.justification: At zero lag the success computation is exactly ordinary ID.
body.gap: ID failure returns unknown because the fixed-alphabet stationary hedge lift is unproved.
body.consumer: Static users recover valid ordinary-ID successes without an unsafe failure claim.
body.proof_tex: If \(L=0\), then \(\gamma=0\).  Refinement span permits only lag-zero directed and shared-root relations.  Exact summary fixes their coordinate pairs to those in \(H\), and instantaneous acyclicity makes the directed part of \(H\) a DAG without a directed self-loop.  The ordered procedure therefore reaches its acyclic branch and its ancestral ADMG is the ordinary finite static ancestral graph for the query \(P(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))\).  It invokes exactly the memoized ordinary ID call specified in \(\mathrm{def:transducer\text{-}handle}\).  If ID returns \(F\), \(\mathrm{prop:acyclic\text{-}summary\text{-}reduction}\) proves that \(F\) is the ordinary ID functional and is uniformly valid on the common product alphabet.  If ID fails, the procedure returns \(\operatorname{UNKNOWN}\) by construction.  No static hedge is claimed to lift to a positive stationary pair on every fixed alphabet.
